newsitem.title: USA: CME Nov lumber falls limit on weak cash market.
newsitem.headline: CME Nov lumber falls limit on weak cash market.

text.p: CME November lumber futures fell the $10.00 per thousand board feet daily trading limit as traders sold the market in response to news of softness in the cash market, trade sources said.
"The cash market is basically flat," said Neil Schmaedick, lumber analyst at Smith Barney. "Nobody's buying anything."
However, traders anticipating bullish data from the Canadian government on lumber export quotas bought November and lifted it off the limit, sources said.
An announcement from the Canadian government could come as early as Thursday, trade sources said.

Cash prices were flat because lumber wholesalers were said to have more on-hand supplies than most in the trade initially thought, and those supplies were weighing on the front-month contracts, trade sources said.
That talk in the market also spurred long liquidation in November by dashing hopes that short postion holders would get caught in a supply squeeze, lumber sources said.
At 0938 CST, November lumber was down $7.20 at $405.00 per tbf and January was down $6.30 at $368.10 per tbf. Other contracts were down $0.60 to to down $2.90 per tbf.
